findings.title: Contexts made the first friendships
findings.body: At W1, 88% of friendship ties joined people who shared a dorm, class section, chat or study group. Shared context is the clearest positive driver in the tie-change model (+0.35 rating points per SD).

findings.title: Gender lines blurred
findings.body: The E-I index for gender went from -0.75 to -0.09 (random mixing would give +0.07). Friendships started almost entirely within gender and became nearly as mixed as chance by the end of semester 2.
findings.theory: Homophily (McPherson et al.), weakening as contact grows

findings.title: Friendships reshuffle every half-semester
findings.body: Only 47%–59% of friendship ties carry over between waves (Jaccard). The biggest loss came at W4: 8 ties lost, 1 gained.
findings.theory: Network churn; Dunbar's limit on close ties

findings.title: Drama follows romance, then spreads through side-taking
findings.body: Hostile ties went from 0 to 5 after the breakup. Tension (share of signed triangles that are unbalanced) peaked at 17% in W3. People caught between two sides at some point: P04, P07.

findings.title: What moves a friendship rating
findings.body: Strongest clear effects: current friendship level (-0.55); shared contexts next wave (+0.35); negative events between them (-0.28); gpa gap (points out of 20) (-0.25). The model explains 49% of rating changes.
findings.theory: Tie-change regression; stand-in for RSiena on the full data

findings.title: Unreciprocated ties are where people get hurt
findings.body: Largest perception gaps at W4: P01 rates P02 3, gets 1 back; P01 rates P03 3, gets 1 back; P08 rates P01 2, gets 0 back.

findings.title: The model beats 'nothing changes', but drama is hard to foresee
findings.body: Predicting each wave from the one before, the tie-level error (Brier) is 0.11 against 0.20 for assuming no change. Started from W1 and run freely, it reproduces density, clustering and gender mixing, but not the number of hostile ties: the breakup cascade is path-dependent.

predictions.title: P06 and P10 start dating
predictions.body: Mutual interest is already reported; both are single.

predictions.title: P03 and P09 break up
predictions.body: Breakup hazard estimated at 0.11 per month (one breakup in W1–W4, shrunk toward a prior).

predictions.title: P07 sides with P09 and drifts from P10
predictions.body: P07 is friends with both P09 and P10, who are hostile. Still caught in the middle at the end of S3: 57%; P09 and P10 reconcile: 0%.

predictions.title: P03 ends S3 with at most one friend
predictions.body: Expected friendships at the end of S3: 0.8.

predictions.title: P01 ends S3 with at most one friend
predictions.body: Expected friendships at the end of S3: 1.5.

predictions.title: New hostility between P03 and P09
predictions.body: They are a couple now; this is the risk that a breakup turns hostile, as the last one did.

predictions.title: Existing hostilities last through S3
predictions.body: Average over the 5 hostile pairs: P09–P10 100%, P08–P09 100%, P03–P08 18%, P03–P04 17%, P03–P10 11%.
